instruction: Open the Booking Assistance and Troubleshooting page on Ticketek's help center.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent started on premier.ticketek.com.au which showed a security block. Tried Google search (SSL error). Eventually navigated to help.ticketek.com.au/hc/en-us, passed Cloudflare CAPTCHA, and found FAQ categories including Booking Assistance and Troubleshooting, Ticket Delivery, Contact Us, etc.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome address bar, enter URLs, handle Cloudflare CAPTCHA, browse help pages, click category links
metadata.failure_analysis: Original task failed due to URL pattern mismatch. Agent demonstrated ability to reach the help center and click category links successfully.
metadata.task_rationale: Variation uses a different FAQ category (Booking Assistance) than the original (Ticket Delivery) to test the same navigation capability. The model demonstrated it can reach the help page and click category links.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the Booking Assistance section on the help site. Evaluator checks URL matches both the help domain and contains 'Booking' in the path. The Booking Assistance category is visible on the help center page the model successfully reached.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active tab URL, which is the right state for verifying a navigation task.

Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly receives the rules dict (via get_rule for type='rule') and iterates over all patterns, requiring ALL to match. Parameter handling is correct: rules['expected'] accesses the pattern list directly.
Pattern 'help\.ticketek\.com\.au' correctly verifies navigation to the Ticketek help center domain.
Pattern '[Bb]ooking' verifies the URL contains 'Booking' (case-flexible), which is expected for the 'Booking Assistance and Troubleshooting' category page.

Minor gap: only 'Booking' is checked, not 'Troubleshooting'. However, since 'Booking Assistance and Troubleshooting' is a single category, matching 'Booking' on the help domain is sufficiently specific and unlikely to produce false positives.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a third pattern like '[Tt]roubleshooting' to more precisely match the full category name, though this is optional since 'Booking' combined with the domain is already specific enough.
